name: Alethrin
manufacturer: Helix Biosystems (disavowed research line, now produced by gray-market chemists using leaked synthesis docs)
description: A neuroactive compound that targets the BCI's prefrontal interface layer, suppressing the neural circuits responsible for intentional deception while leaving cognition and memory intact. Under Alethrin, subjects cannot generate deliberate falsehoods — they can refuse to speak, but any statement they make will be true as they believe it. Helix developed it for 'enhanced compliance therapy' before the project was publicly disavowed; the synthesis documents leaked within a year.
effects: pharmacological suppression of deliberate deception via BCI prefrontal override
subject experiences deception attempts as physically painful — burning sensation behind the eyes
enhances interrogator's BCI read of stress markers for verification
side_effects: subjects with hardened BCI firewall implants may partially resist — reduced to half-truths and omissions rather than full suppression
severe psychological distress during active effect
post-dose: 30% of subjects experience 4-8 hours of compulsive truth-telling even after compound clears — cannot stop volunteering information
repeated use causes permanent reduction in capacity for social deception (blunted affect, social dysfunction)
contraindicated with Nullform or any BCI-isolation drug — interaction causes seizure
cultural_context: The interrogation tool of choice for mid-tier corporate security, information brokers, and organized crime lieutenants who need answers fast and clean. The irony in GLMZ is that Alethrin is considered a 'polite' interrogation method — no physical damage, no screaming. Operators who use it often tell themselves they're being humane. Subjects disagree. The post-dose compulsive truth-telling effect has ruined careers, marriages, and cover identities.
story_hooks: A corporate spy is dosed with Alethrin during a routine security check — they don't know it. They answer every question honestly, including ones about operations their handler told them to protect. Now both the spy and the handler are burned.
An information broker sells Alethrin-derived intelligence to three different clients, all of whom are now looking for the source. The broker realizes they may have sold their own location.
A Tier 3 defense attorney discovers their client was Alethrin-dosed during a corpo 'voluntary interview' — the confession is inadmissible, but the corps already acted on the information.
